Additionally, please pay attention to the mattress material, which is especially important for people with allergies or sensitivities, as well as the warranty terms provided by the manufacturer, which are often an indicator of quality. A good mattress can last 8 to 10 years; this is a long-term investment, so please take your time to choose carefully.
text_tgt_raw: 在選擇床墊時，這項為您睡眠品質重要的決定，請先考慮最適合您睡姿的軟硬度。如果您習慣仰睡，這也是最常見的睡姿，一張中等偏硬的床墊會是理想的選擇，它能提供足夠支撐而不會過於僵硬。然而，對於側睡者來說，為避免肩膀和臀部承受過多壓力，一張較軟且具服貼性的床墊，像是記憶棉床墊，通常是最好的。別忘了在店裡試躺至少10到15分鐘，而不只是坐著，如此才能確保這張床墊真的讓您感到舒適。此外，也請留意床墊的材質，這對於有過敏或敏感體質的人來說格外重要，還有製造商提供的保固條款，這往往是品質的指標。一張好的床墊可用上8到10年，這是一項長期的投資，因此請您花時間仔細挑選。
base_en: When choosing a mattress—an important decision for your rest—consider 1st the type of firmness that best suits your sleeping posture. If you sleep on your back—the most common position—a medium-firm mattress could be ideal, offering support without excessive rigidity. For those who sleep on their side—thus avoiding pressure on shoulders and hips—a softer, more adaptable mattress, like a memory foam one, is often the best option. Don't forget to try the mattress in the store for at least 10 or 15 minutes—don't just sit on it—to make sure it's really comfortable for you. Also check the materials—important for allergies or sensitivities—and the warranties offered by manufacturers—an indicator of quality. A good mattress can last between 8 and 10 years—a long-term investment—so take your time to choose well.

text_es: Reducing food waste is a major global issue, crucial for the planet's sustainable development and food security. It's estimated that about one-third of the food produced annually, or up to 1.3 billion tons, is ultimately discarded or wasted, which has serious economic, social, and environmental impacts. To address this problem, we should develop more conscious consumption habits, such as properly planning purchases, effectively using leftover ingredients, and learning how to correctly store food to extend its shelf life and prevent premature spoilage. Furthermore, thoroughly understanding expiration dates and best-by dates is also very important. From production to distribution, the food industry plays a key role in optimizing processes and reducing losses, and public policies that encourage the donation of edible food are equally important. Even a small individual action like not throwing away perfectly good food will have a positive collective impact overall, allowing us to work together, here and there, to reduce unnecessary waste.
text_tgt_raw: 減少廚餘是全球性重大議題，對於地球永續發展與糧食安全至關重要。據估計，每年生產的食物約有三分之一，亦即高達十三億噸，最終被丟棄或浪費，這對經濟、社會和環境都造成了嚴重影響。為了解決這個問題，我們應養成更為有意識的消費習慣，例如妥善規劃採買、有效利用剩餘食材，並學習如何正確儲存食物以延長保鮮期，避免提早腐敗。此外，徹底理解保存期限與最佳賞味期也十分重要。從生產到配送，食品產業在優化製程與減少損耗方面扮演著關鍵角色，而鼓勵捐贈可食用食物的公共政策也同等重要。即便只是不丟棄狀況良好的食物這樣一個小小的個人舉動，都將為整體帶來正面的集體影響，讓我們在這裡、在那裡，共同努力減少不必要的浪費。
base_en: Reducing food waste—a global problem of great magnitude—is crucial for the planet's sustainability and food security. It's estimated that 1/3 of all food produced annually is lost or wasted—approximately 1.3 billion tons—which has serious economic, social, and environmental implications. Combating this involves adopting more conscious consumption habits—such as planning purchases and utilizing surpluses—properly storing food to extend its shelf life—thus preventing its premature spoilage—and thoroughly understanding expiration and best-by dates. The role of the food industry—from production to distribution—is also fundamental in optimizing its processes and minimizing losses, as are public policies that encourage the donation of food suitable for consumption. Every small individual gesture—like not discarding food in good condition—contributes to a positive collective impact.

text_es: Ever since I became aware of the impact of human behavior on the environment a few years ago, reducing food waste has become a top priority in my household. I remember one time, I cooked dinner for eight friends, which was a culinary challenge in itself, and the leftovers were enough for three days, which made me feel terrible. From then on, I learned to plan menus more precisely in advance and only buy necessary ingredients, which helped me avoid impulse purchases—I admit that's my weakness. I also developed the habit of creatively repurposing leftovers; for example, a simple stew could transform into delicious croquettes the next day. Honestly, I discovered an unexpected cooking talent because of this. I firmly believe that even the most insignificant changes in daily life can make a huge impact. Now, when I see leftover food, I think, "How can I give it a second life?" This is a question I'm happy to answer.
text_tgt_raw: 自從幾年前我開始意識到人類行為對環境的影響以來，減少廚餘便成了我家裡的首要任務。我記得有一次，我為八位朋友準備晚餐，這本身就是一項烹飪挑戰，結果剩下的菜餚足夠吃三天，那讓我覺得非常糟糕。從那裡開始，我學著事先更精確地規劃菜單，只購買必要的食材，如此一來便能避免衝動購物——我承認這是我的弱點。我也養成了將剩菜創意再利用的習慣，例如一道簡單的燉菜，隔天就能搖身一變成為美味可樂餅。說真的，我為此發現了自己意想不到的烹飪天賦。我堅信，日常生活中即使是再微不足道的改變，也能帶來巨大的影響。現在，當我看到還有剩餘的食物時，我會想：「我能如何為它賦予第二次生命呢？」這是一個我樂於回答的問題。
base_en: Ever since I started becoming more aware—some years ago now—of the environmental impact of our actions, reducing food waste has become a priority in my home. I remember 1 time I organized a dinner for 8 friends—which is always a culinary challenge—and ended up with leftovers for 3 days, something that made me feel terrible. From then on, I started planning menus in advance—and with much more precision—and buying only what was necessary, thus avoiding impulse purchases—which are my downfall, I confess. I've also adopted the habit of creatively reusing leftovers—a simple stew can be transformed into croquettes the next day—and the truth is, I discovered a hidden talent for resourceful cooking. I firmly believe that small changes in our daily habits—however insignificant they may seem—can make a big difference. Now, when I see that there's some food left, I think, "How can I give this a 2nd life?"—a question I enjoy answering.

text_es: To reduce the growing global problem of food waste, we can start with our daily habits. First, it's essential to plan menus in advance and make a shopping list based on your needs, strictly adhering to it to avoid impulsive purchases. Second, proper food storage is very important. For example, store fruits and vegetables separately to extend their shelf life, and regularly check the ingredients in your refrigerator and pantry, prioritizing the use of products that are nearing their expiration date. If you still have fresh ingredients, such as some vegetables that are starting to soften, you can consider freezing them or using them to make broth, soup, or stew. Additionally, creatively reusing leftovers not only saves money but also significantly reduces resource waste. When cooking, pay special attention to portion sizes, especially for one or two people, to avoid cooking too much. If there is still food left over, consider sharing it with others or composting it, which is an excellent eco-friendly option.
text_tgt_raw: 為減少全球日益嚴重的食物浪費問題，我們可以從日常習慣著手。首先，務必事先規劃好菜單，並依照需求列出購物清單，嚴格遵守不隨意購買，避免衝動消費。再來，正確的食物保存方式非常重要，例如將蔬果妥善分開存放，以延長其保鮮期，並定期檢查冰箱和儲藏室裡頭的食材，優先使用快過期的產品。如果還有新鮮食材，例如有些軟爛的蔬菜，這裡我們可以考慮將它們冷凍起來，或是製作成高湯、湯品或燉菜。此外，發揮創意將剩菜剩飯重新利用，不僅能省下金錢，也能大幅減少資源浪費。在烹飪時，應特別注意份量，尤其是一到兩人的用餐，避免烹煮過多。若真的仍有剩餘，可考慮與他人分享，或是將其製作成堆肥，這不失為一個極佳的環保選擇。
base_en: To reduce food waste—a serious global problem—start by planning your meals in advance, making a shopping list—only of what you need—and sticking to it strictly to avoid impulse purchases. It's essential to store food correctly—separating fruits and vegetables according to their needs—to prolong its shelf life, and to regularly check the fridge and pantry to use the oldest products 1st. If you've leftover fresh ingredients—for example, vegetables that are starting to wilt—think about freezing them or turning them into broths, soups, or stews. Also, use leftovers—creatively, of course—in other meals; this way you not only save money, but you also minimize the waste of valuable food. Also consider portion sizes—especially when cooking for 1 or 2 people—to avoid overcooking, and if you still have leftovers, share them or think about composting—an excellent ecological option—as a 3rd alternative.

text_es: Learning to swim as an adult, though sometimes challenging, is a rewarding process that offers numerous benefits for both physical and mental well-being. Many people, for various reasons, did not learn this skill in childhood, but adulthood is by no means an obstacle to acquiring this important ability. Adult classes typically focus on overcoming fear of water (a common barrier) and developing basic floating and propulsion techniques. With patience and consistent practice, usually two to three times a week, significant progress can be made in a short amount of time. Besides being a survival skill, swimming is also a low-impact exercise (ideal for joints) and an excellent way to relieve stress, thereby enhancing overall well-being. No matter how old you are, it's never too late to learn to swim; it will open up a vast world of recreational and exercise opportunities for you.
text_tgt_raw: 成年後學習游泳，儘管有時充滿挑戰，卻是一段收穫豐盛的過程，為身心健康帶來諸多益處。許多人因著各種原因，童年裡未能習得此項技能，但成年絕非學習這項重要能力的阻礙。成人課程通常著重於克服對水的恐懼（這是一個常見的障礙），並發展基本的漂浮與推進技巧。憑藉著耐心和持續練習，通常每週兩到三次，短時間內便能取得顯著進步。游泳除了是生存技能外，更是一種低衝擊的運動（對關節而言極為理想），同時也是釋放壓力的絕佳方式，進而提升整體幸福感。無論年紀多大，學習游泳永不嫌遲，它將為您開啟一個充滿休閒與運動機會的廣闊世界。
base_en: Learning to swim as an adult is a rewarding—though sometimes challenging—experience that offers numerous benefits for physical and mental health. Many people—for various reasons—didn't have the opportunity to learn in childhood, but adulthood isn't an impediment to acquiring this vital skill. Courses for adults usually focus on overcoming the fear of water—a common obstacle—and on developing basic floating and propulsion techniques. With patience and constant practice—generally 2 or 3 sessions per week—significant progress can be made in a short time. In addition to being a survival skill, swimming is a low-impact exercise—ideal for the joints—and an excellent way to release stress—which improves overall well-being. No matter the age—it's never too late to start—swimming opens up a world of opportunities for leisure and sport.

text_es: Last year I turned thirty-five, which is a bit late to learn how to swim, but I still decided it was time. In the past, I always tried to avoid water, even in the summer, and this fear greatly limited my enjoyment of vacations, especially at the beach. So I signed up for an adult swimming class at the municipal pool, and everyone in the class was like me, each with some fear of water. It was really frustrating at first, and a little embarrassing, but my coach was a very patient and experienced teacher who constantly encouraged me. After three months of hard work, I finally learned to float and completed my first swim in my life, and the feeling was incredible! Now I really enjoy being in the water and even dare to try the backstroke.
text_tgt_raw: 去年我三十五歲，對學游泳來說，這年紀算是偏晚了些，但我還是決定是時候該學游泳了。過去我總會盡量避開水，即使是夏天也一樣，這份恐懼大大地限制了我度假的樂趣，尤其是在海邊的時候。於是我報名了市立游泳池的成人游泳班，班裡的人都和我一樣，各自懷著一些對水的恐懼。一開始真的很令人挫折，也稍微有點尷尬，但我的教練是一位非常有耐心且經驗豐富的老師，他不斷鼓勵著我。經過三個月的努力，我終於學會了漂浮，也完成了我人生中的第一次游泳，那種感覺真是不可思議！現在我非常享受待在水裡，甚至敢嘗試仰式了。
base_en: Last year, at 35 years old—a somewhat advanced age to start—I decided it was time to learn how to swim. I had always avoided water—even in summer—and that phobia greatly limited me on vacations—especially at the beach. I signed up for swimming lessons with a group of adults—all with our fears—at the municipal pool. At 1st it was frustrating—and a little embarrassing—but my instructor, a very patient man—with decades of experience—encouraged me to continue. After 3 months of effort, I managed to float and do my 1st laps—an incredible feeling! Now I enjoy the water and even dare to do some backstrokes.

text_es: If you are considering learning to swim as an adult, a fundamental yet life-enriching skill, then starting with professional lessons is crucial. Be sure to find a patient and experienced excellent instructor, especially one who can understand and address the common fear of water among adults. To begin, practice in the shallow end of the pool, where you can feel safe, and first get familiar with breathing and buoyancy before attempting more complex movements. Persistence is the key to success—practice regularly to solidify your progress, and don't get discouraged even if you don't see immediate results, as everyone learns at a different pace. You can find videos and information on kicking and stroking techniques from the abundant resources online, and you will discover that with time and effort, you can master being in the water and fully enjoy the physical and mental benefits that swimming brings.
text_tgt_raw: 如果您正考慮成年後學習游泳這項既基本又豐富人生的技能，那麼從專業課程開始著手是至關重要的。請務必尋找一位耐心且經驗豐富的優良教練，尤其需要能理解並處理成人普遍存在的恐水心理。一開始，在泳池淺水區練習，那裡能讓您感到安全，並先熟悉呼吸和浮力，再嘗試更複雜的動作。持之以恆是成功的關鍵——定期練習以鞏固您的進步，即使沒有立即見效也別氣餒，每個人的學習步調都不一樣。您可以從網路上的豐富資源裡獲取關於打水和划手技巧的影片與資料，您會發現只要付出時間和努力，便能掌握水性，盡情享受游泳帶來的身心益處。
base_en: If you're thinking about learning to swim as an adult—a fundamental and enriching skill—it's crucial to start with specialized classes. Look for a good instructor—someone with patience and experience—who knows how to handle fear of water, something very common in adults. Start in the shallow end of the pool—where you feel safe—and familiarize yourself with breathing and floating before attempting more complex movements. Consistency is key—practice regularly to solidify your progress—and don't get discouraged if you don't see immediate results; everyone has their own pace. Gather tips on kicking and stroking techniques—there are many online resources that can help you—and you'll see that, with time and effort, you'll master the water and enjoy all its benefits—both physical and mental.

text_es: To give a space a new look, painting the walls is a relatively simple renovation method that can completely change the home's atmosphere, instantly bringing a bright, refreshed feeling. Before starting the work, preparation is crucial. We must carefully cover furniture and floors to avoid paint splatters, which is a key step to ensure a flawless final result. Next, the choice of paint color is a very important part of aesthetic consideration, as it directly affects our perception of the room's size and lighting. Therefore, it is recommended to test colors first to ensure you select the most ideal shade. After completing the preliminary preparations, if needed, a primer will then be applied. This improves paint adhesion and helps the final color be more uniform, especially on new or porous surfaces. Finally, two to three coats of paint are usually applied, with the recommended drying time—typically several hours—between each coat to achieve a professional and long-lasting perfect finish.
text_tgt_raw: 為空間換上新裝，粉刷牆面可說是一種相對簡單卻能徹底改變居家氛圍的裝修方式，瞬間帶來煥然一新的明亮感。在開始動工之前，準備工作至關重要，我們必須仔細將家具和地板覆蓋好，以避免油漆飛濺，這也是確保最終成果完美無瑕的關鍵一步。再來，油漆顏色的選擇為美學考量裡相當重要的一環，它會直接影響我們對房間大小和採光的感受；因此，建議先試色，以確保選到最理想的色調。完成事前準備後，若有需要，接著便會塗上底漆，這能讓油漆附著力更好，也能讓最終色彩更均勻，特別是在全新的或多孔的表面上。最後，通常會漆上兩到三層油漆，每一層之間都得間隔建議的乾燥時間——通常為數小時——才能呈現出專業且持久的完美質感。
base_en: Painting a room is a relatively simple home improvement project that can completely transform the look of a space, bringing a new atmosphere and brightness. Before starting, it's essential to prepare the room—covering furniture and floors—to avoid paint splatters, a key step for a good finish. The choice of paint color—an important aesthetic factor—will influence the perception of the room's size and lighting, making it advisable to test samples to ensure the desired shade. After preparation, primer is applied—if necessary—to ensure better adhesion and uniformity of the final color, especially on new or very porous surfaces. Finally, 2, or 3 coats of paint are applied, allowing the recommended drying time between them—normally several hours—to obtain a professional and durable finish.

text_es: Two months ago, on a whim, I decided it was time to change the color of my bedroom walls. To be honest, the original color of those walls was truly nothing to write home about; that highly saturated shade always reminded me of my first-grade classroom, and living there was truly unpleasant. I bought a can of beautiful off-white paint and gathered all the tools, naively thinking at the time that it would be an easy job. The first day went smoothly, but by the second day, my arms couldn't be lifted anymore—admit it, I'm inherently lazy. Fortunately, my sister arrived just in time to rescue me; her skillful hands in this area are much better than mine. The two of us worked on it for three afternoons and finally finished the job. The final result, to be honest, had ninety percent of the effort coming from her; this room is now completely refreshed, brighter and cozier, and it feels like we really accomplished something. Now, all that's left is to enjoy this new space, and of course, be careful not to get the walls dirty.
text_tgt_raw: 兩個月前，我心血來潮，覺得是時候替臥室牆壁換個顏色了。老實說，那牆面原本的顏色實在令人不敢恭維，那種飽和度極高的色調，總讓我想起小學一年級的教室，在這裡居住著真不是滋味。我買了罐漂亮的米白色油漆，也備齊了所有工具，當時還天真地以為這會是件輕鬆差事。第一天進度順利，然而到了第二天，我的手臂卻再也舉不起來了——承認吧，我骨子裡就是懶散。幸運的是，我妹妹及時趕來救援，她這方面的巧手可是比我強上許多。我們倆人為此奮鬥了三個下午，終於大功告成。最終的成果，說真的，有百分之九十的努力都來自於她，這間房間如今煥然一新，變得更加明亮且溫馨，感覺我們真的做到了。現在，就等著好好享受這個新空間了，當然，可得小心別把牆弄髒。
base_en: 2 months ago, I decided it was time to paint my bedroom. The truth—and I'm not saying this to discourage anyone—is that the wall had a pretty ugly color, a shade that reminded me of 1st grade. I bought the paint—a beautiful off-white—and all the necessary tools, convinced it would be an easy task. The 1st day went well, but by the 2nd day, my arms couldn't take it anymore—I'm a bit lazy, I admit. Fortunately, my sister came to help me—she's handier than I'm—and between the 2 of us, we finished it in 3 afternoons. The final result—with 90% of her effort, honestly—was spectacular, and the room looks completely different, much brighter and cozier—we did it, yes. Now all that's left is to enjoy it—and not get the walls dirty.

text_es: When you're ready to repaint a room, this job, while very rewarding, requires thorough planning beforehand. Before you begin, please ensure all materials are ready, such as paint, brushes, rollers, painter's tape, and drop cloths. First, carefully prepare the walls by cleaning dirt and repairing imperfections, then protect the floor and furniture with drop cloths. Using good quality painter's tape is very important because cheap tape might peel off the paint when removed; carefully apply it along the edges of the ceiling, baseboards, door frames, and window frames. To achieve an even and durable paint finish, two coats are recommended, and three coats can be considered if there's a significant color difference. Additionally, during and after painting, please ensure good ventilation indoors, as health is paramount. Finally, take your time, enjoy the entire process, and don't rush.
text_tgt_raw: 當您準備為房間重新上漆時，這份工作雖然很有成就感，但事前周全的規劃是首要之務。在著手進行前，請確保所有材料都已備齊，例如油漆、刷子、滾筒、遮蔽膠帶和防護塑膠布。首先要仔細處理牆面，清潔髒污並修補瑕疵，接著用防塵布保護好地板和家具。使用品質好的遮蔽膠帶非常重要，因為廉價的膠帶可能會在撕下時連同漆面剝落，請仔細沿著天花板、踢腳板、門框及窗框邊緣貼好。為了獲得均勻且持久的漆面，建議上兩層漆，若顏色差異較大則可考慮三層。此外，在粉刷期間及完工後，請務必保持室內通風良好，畢竟健康為首。最後，請放慢腳步，享受整個過程，切勿操之過急。
base_en: When you start painting a room—a rewarding task—the 1st thing is good planning. Make sure you've all the materials—paint, brushes, rollers, painter's tape, protective plastic sheets—on hand before you begin. Prepare the surface well—clean the walls, repair any imperfections—and protect the floor and furniture with drop cloths. Use good quality painter's tape—cheap tape can peel off paint—to define the edges of ceilings, baseboards, and door and window frames. Apply 2 coats of paint—or 3, if the color is very different—for a uniform and durable finish. Don't forget to ventilate the space well—health comes 1st—during and after painting. Finally, take your time—haste isn't a good advisor—and enjoy the process.

text_es: Beginning meditation, an ancient practice, primarily involves dedicating time to train the mind to achieve states of mindfulness and deep relaxation. It requires no prior experience, anyone can start, and the benefits can become apparent in a short period. Ideally, we should find a quiet, undisturbed place and adopt a comfortable sitting or lying position. You can start with short periods of five to ten minutes daily, then gradually increase the length of your meditation as you become more comfortable with the process. The main goal here is to observe thoughts without judgment, allowing them to pass naturally, and using your breath as an anchor. This regular practice brings benefits to both body and mind, effectively reducing stress, improving concentration, and cultivating deeper self-awareness.
text_tgt_raw: 開始冥想這項古老的練習，主要在於投入時間訓練心靈，以達到正念和深度放鬆的狀態。這不需要任何先前的經驗，任何人都能著手進行，且好處在短時間裡就能顯現。理想上，我們應尋找一處寧靜、不受干擾的地方，並採取坐著或躺著的舒適姿勢。您可以從每天五到十分鐘的短時間開始，然後隨著對此過程感到更自在，逐步增加冥想的長度。這裡的主要目標是觀察思緒而不加以評判，讓它們自然地流逝，並將呼吸作為錨點。這種規律的練習，為身心帶來益處，能有效減輕壓力、提升專注力，並培養更深層的自我覺察。
base_en: Starting to meditate—an ancient practice—involves dedicating time to train the mind to achieve a state of mindfulness and deep relaxation. No prior experience is required—anyone can start—and the benefits can be noticeable in a short time. The ideal is to find a quiet place—free from distractions—and establish a comfortable posture, either sitting or lying down. You can start with short sessions—5 to 10 minutes a day—and gradually increase the duration as you feel more comfortable with the process. The main goal is to observe thoughts without judging them—simply letting them pass—and focusing on the breath as an anchor. This regular practice—which benefits body and mind—can reduce stress, improve concentration, and foster greater self-awareness.

text_es: I still remember the first time I tried meditation five years ago; it was an absolute disaster. I sat on the floor, and that cushion was really uncomfortable. I thought I'd be able to relax, but my mind was like a party. Worries about my shopping list (oh no, did I buy milk?), unfinished work, and even that catchy tune I hated kept popping up. I tried to focus on my breathing, a method I'd read about in an online blog, but each inhale and exhale felt very unnatural. After about ten minutes, though it felt like two hours, I finally gave up, feeling very frustrated and even more stressed than before I started meditating. At the time, I thought meditation wasn't for me, which is perhaps a common thought, but I decided to give myself another chance the next day.
text_tgt_raw: 我還記得五年前第一次嘗試冥想時，簡直是一場災難。我坐在地板上，那個坐墊著實不太舒服，原以為能好好放鬆，但腦袋裡卻像在開派對。購物清單的煩惱（糟糕，我到底有沒有買牛奶？）、懸而未決的工作，甚至連那首我討厭卻又很洗腦的旋律，都在那裡不斷地湧現。我試著把注意力放在呼吸上，這是在某個網路部落格裡讀到的方法，但每次吸氣和吐氣都感覺很不自然。大約十分鐘後，雖然感覺像過了兩小時，我最終放棄了，感到非常沮喪，壓力甚至比冥想前更大。當時我認為冥想不適合我，這或許是很普遍的想法，但我決定隔天再給自己一次機會。
base_en: I remember that my 1st attempt to meditate—5 years ago now—was an absolute disaster. I sat on the floor—on a rather uncomfortable cushion—with the idea of relaxing, but my mind seemed to be having a party. Thoughts about the shopping list—what a disaster, I couldn't remember if I had milk!—the pending work, and even the melody of a catchy song—the one I hated, too—crowded in incessantly. I tried to focus on my breathing—a tip I had read on a blog—but each inhalation and exhalation felt forced. After about 10 minutes—which felt like 2 hours—I gave up, frustrated, and more stressed than before. I thought that meditation wasn't for me—a pretty common idea, I suppose—but I decided to give it another chance the next day.

text_es: If you want to start practicing meditation, which is a habit that greatly benefits both mind and body, first find a quiet place where you won't be disturbed. You can sit comfortably, whether on a chair or a cushion, keeping your back straight but relaxed. Next, focus your attention on your breath, feeling how air enters and leaves your body; this is the foundation of meditation practice. If your mind starts to wander, which is quite natural when you're just starting, don't get discouraged; simply and gently guide your attention back to your breath. It's recommended to start with short practice sessions, such as five to ten minutes, and then as you gradually feel more comfortable, you can slowly increase the meditation time, up to twenty or thirty minutes daily. The key here is consistency; even practicing only three times a week will be helpful, rather than striving for perfection; each practice session is an opportunity to cultivate mindfulness.
text_tgt_raw: 若想開始練習冥想，這是一個對身心極有益處的習慣，首先要找一個不被打擾的安靜地方。您可以舒服地坐著，無論是在椅子上或墊子上，保持背部挺直但放鬆。接著，將注意力專注在您的呼吸上，感受空氣如何進出體內，這是冥想練習的基礎。如果思緒開始遊走，這在剛開始時是相當自然的，請不要為此感到沮喪；只需溫和地將注意力再次引導回呼吸即可。建議從短時間的練習開始，例如五到十分鐘，然後隨著您漸漸感到更自在，可以慢慢增加冥想的時間，直到每天二、三十分鐘。這裡的關鍵在於持之以恆，即使一週只練習三次，也會有所幫助，而不是追求完美；每一次的練習都是一個培養正念的機會。
base_en: To start meditating—a very beneficial habit—find a quiet place where you won't be disturbed. Sit comfortably—in a chair or on a cushion—with your back straight but relaxed. Concentrate on your breath—the anchor of your practice—feeling how the air enters and leaves. Don't get frustrated if your mind wanders—it's completely normal at 1st—; simply gently redirect your attention to your breath each time. Start with short sessions, 5, or 10 minutes, and gradually increase the duration—when you feel more comfortable—until you reach 20 or 30 minutes a day. The key is consistency—even 3 days a week make a difference—not perfection; each session is an opportunity to practice mindfulness.

text_es: Preparing for an interview is an extremely critical step in the job search process, and it includes several important stages to maximize your chances of success. First, be sure to thoroughly research the company and the position, understanding its mission, values, and products, so you can tailor your answers. Next, you should review your resume and be familiar with the dates and achievements listed on it, while also being prepared to provide reasonable explanations for every point mentioned in your cover letter. You should also anticipate various questions, whether typical or more challenging, and practice your answers out loud, preferably in front of a mirror or with a friend. Additionally, it's important to prepare some insightful questions to ask the interviewer, as this demonstrates your interest and initiative. Finally, dress appropriately and arrive on time (about 10 to 15 minutes early); these details will significantly add to your advantage.
text_tgt_raw: 準備面試是求職過程中極為關鍵的一步，為著能最大化成功機會，裡頭包含了幾個重要階段。首先，務必徹底研究該公司及其職位，了解其使命、價值觀與產品，以便量身打造回答內容。接著，應回顧履歷並熟悉其上所載的日期及成就，同時也要準備好為你的自薦信裡提及的每個要點提供合理解釋。你還應預想各種問題，無論是典型的或是較具挑戰性的，並大聲練習回答，最好是照著鏡子或與朋友一起練習。此外，準備一些有深度的問題來問面試官也很重要，這能展現你的興趣與積極主動。最後，穿著得體的服裝，並準時（約提前10到15分鐘）抵達，這些細節都會為你加分不少。
base_en: Preparing for a job interview—a crucial step in the job search—involves several key phases to maximize the chances of success. 1st, it's essential to thoroughly research the company and the position—knowing its mission, values, and products—to tailor your answers. Then, you need to review your resume—memorizing dates and achievements—and cover letter, being prepared to justify each point. You should also anticipate possible questions—both typical and more challenging ones—and practice your answers out loud—preferably in front of a mirror or with a friend. It's important to prepare intelligent questions for the interviewer—demonstrating interest and proactivity—at the end of the interview. Finally, appropriate attire—professional and neat—and arriving on time—about 10 or 15 minutes early—are details that make a big difference.

text_es: Yesterday, I spent three hours preparing for my long-awaited software development job interview. The first thing I did was thoroughly research the company—its mission and values—as well as the detailed description of the position I applied for, ensuring I understood every detail. Next, I reviewed my resume and relevant experience point by point, mentally formulating specific examples that could demonstrate my abilities. To be able to express myself clearly and confidently, I also practiced answering some common questions in front of a mirror, such as "Why do you want this position?" These preparations truly benefited me greatly. Finally, I prepared some questions to ask them, which is necessary to show interest in the position, and selected the outfit I would wear on the interview day, making sure it was both formal and comfortable. I hope everything goes well!
text_tgt_raw: 為了我期待已久的軟體開發職位面試，昨天我花了三個小時準備。我做的第一件事，就是徹底研究這間公司—它的宗旨與價值觀—以及我應徵職位的詳細介紹，確保理解每個細節。接著，我逐點審閱了自己的履歷與相關經驗，腦中構思著能佐證我能力的具體範例。為了能夠清晰且自信地表達，我還對著鏡子練習回答一些常見問題，像是「你為什麼想獲得這個職位？」這些準備著實讓我受益良多。最後，我準備了一些問題要問他們，這對於展現對職位的興趣是為必要，並且挑選了面試當天要穿的服裝，既要正式也得舒適。期盼一切順利！
base_en: Yesterday I spent 3 hours preparing for a job interview—the one I've been waiting for—for a software development position. The 1st thing I did was thoroughly research the company—its mission and values—and the profile of the position I was applying for, making sure to understand every detail. Afterward, I reviewed my own resume—point by point—and my relevant experiences, thinking of concrete examples I could use to illustrate my skills. I also practiced my answers to common questions—like "Why do you want this position?"—in front of the mirror, aiming for clear and confident articulation. Finally, I prepared some questions to ask them—essential for showing interest—and chose the appropriate clothing—formal, but comfortable—for the big day. Fingers crossed for success.

text_es: To prepare thoroughly for a critical job interview, you need to be fully ready. First, be sure to research the company in depth, understand its corporate culture and core values, and carefully analyze the position you aspire to, grasping its main responsibilities. Next, review your resume, identify your strengths, and prepare specific examples (such as STAR situations) to demonstrate your relevant skills and extensive experience. At the same time, prepare answers to common interview questions in advance, including how to explain your weaknesses, and prepare two to three in-depth questions for the interviewer that demonstrate your proactive attitude. On the day of the interview, be sure to arrive 10 to 15 minutes early, dress professionally and appropriately, and maintain a positive and confident attitude throughout the process, which will open a new chapter in your career.
text_tgt_raw: 為了一場關鍵的求職面試，您需要做好萬全準備。首先，請務必深入研究該公司，了解其企業文化與核心價值觀，並仔細分析您所嚮往的職位，掌握其主要職責。接著，檢視自己的履歷，找出其中的優勢，並準備好具體的實例（例如STAR情境），來展現您的相關技能與豐富經驗。同時，預先準備好常見面試問題的答案，包括如何說明您的弱點，並為面試官準備兩到三個有深度、能展現您積極態度的提問。面試當天，請務必提早10到15分鐘抵達，穿著專業得體，並在整個過程中保持積極自信的態度，這將為您的職場生涯開啟新的篇章。
base_en: To prepare for a job interview—a crucial step in your career—thoroughly research the company—its culture and values—and the position you aspire to—its key responsibilities. Review your resume—identifying strengths—and think of concrete examples—STAR situations—that demonstrate your relevant skills and experience. Prepare answers to common questions—for example, about your weaknesses—and also formulate 2 or 3 intelligent questions for the interviewer—this shows genuine interest. Make sure to arrive on time—10 or 15 minutes early—dress professionally, and maintain a positive and confident attitude throughout the entire process.

text_es: When building a campfire during outdoor activities, following a series of important steps is essential to ensure safety and protect the environment. First, you must choose a suitable location, away from dry vegetation, trees, and buildings, and clear an area at least three meters in diameter, removing fallen leaves, branches, and any flammable materials. It is recommended to surround the campfire area with rocks to form an effective barrier to prevent the fire from spreading, and to always have water or a fire extinguisher readily available. Remember, never leave a campfire unattended, not even for a moment. Afterward, be sure to ensure that the embers are completely extinguished and cold to the touch; this is a crucial step for safety. Additionally, it is important to check local regulations, as fires may be prohibited here or there during certain periods; also avoid lighting fires on windy days. Ultimately, a sense of personal responsibility—an unavoidable value in natural environments—is the best tool for enjoying the pleasure of a campfire without risk.
text_tgt_raw: 在戶外活動裡生營火時，為確保安全並保護環境，遵循一系列重要步驟是不可或缺的。首先，必須選擇一處合適的地點，遠離乾燥植被、樹木和建築物，並清理出至少三公尺直徑的範圍，移除落葉、樹枝及任何易燃物。建議用石頭圍住營火區，形成有效的屏障以防止火勢蔓延，同時手邊隨時準備著水或滅火器。切記，絕不能讓營火無人看管，哪怕只是一瞬間。結束後，務必確保餘燼完全熄滅且觸摸時已冰冷，這是保障安全的關鍵一步。此外，查詢當地法規也很重要，因為這裡或那裡在特定時段可能禁止生火；同時也要避免在刮風的日子點燃。最終，個人責任感——這在自然環境裡是不可避免的價值——才是享受營火樂趣而無風險的最佳工具。
base_en: Making a safe bonfire—a vital practice for any outdoor activity—requires following a series of key steps to prevent fires and protect the environment. 1st, it's essential to choose a suitable location—away from dry vegetation, trees, and structures—and clear an area of at least 3 meters in diameter, removing leaves, branches, and any flammable material. It's advisable to surround the area with stones to contain the fire—an effective barrier against spread—and always have water or a fire extinguisher on hand. You should never leave a bonfire unattended—not even for a brief moment—and, when finished, you must ensure that the embers are completely extinguished and cold to the touch—a crucial step for safety. In addition, it's important to inquire about local regulations—in many places they're prohibited at certain times—and avoid lighting them on windy days. Finally, personal responsibility—an unavoidable value in nature—is the best tool for enjoying a bonfire without risks.

text_es: That summer night, to celebrate my cousin's birthday, we decided to hold my favorite countryside activity—a bonfire party. First, we carefully chose a suitable spot in an open area, far from trees and bushes, to ensure there was no vegetation that could catch fire nearby. Next, with the help of my always cautious dad, we used large rocks to create a safety perimeter at least three meters in diameter. We collected dry fallen branches for firewood, making sure not to cut down any trees, only picking up what had fallen to the ground. Before lighting the fire, we also carefully checked for strong winds to prevent embers from scattering. We cautiously lit the bonfire with paper and kindling, and always kept a bucket of water nearby, just in case. There, we fully enjoyed the warmth of the bonfire and the joy of sharing stories, but safety was undoubtedly our top priority.
text_tgt_raw: 那個夏日夜晚，為了慶祝表弟的生日，我們決定舉辦一場我最喜歡的鄉間活動——營火晚會。首先，我們在遠離樹木和灌木叢的空地上，謹慎地選擇了合適的地點，以確保周圍沒有可能著火的植被。接著，在向來小心謹慎的爸爸協助下，我們用大石頭圍出了一個直徑至少三公尺的安全範圍。我們收集了乾燥的枯枝作為柴火，過程中堅持不砍伐樹木，只撿拾掉落在地上的。點火前，我們也仔細檢查是否會刮起強風，避免火星四散。我們小心翼翼地用紙和引火物點燃營火，並且隨時準備著一桶水在旁邊，以防萬一。在那裡，我們盡情享受著營火帶來的溫暖與分享故事的樂趣，但安全毫無疑問是我們最優先的考量。
base_en: That summer night, we decided to make a bonfire—my favorite activity in the countryside—to celebrate my cousin's birthday. The 1st thing we did was choose the right place—a clearing without nearby vegetation—far from trees and bushes that could catch fire. Then, with the help of my father—always cautious—we marked off the area with large stones, creating a safe circle of at least 3 meters in diameter. We gathered dry firewood—fallen branches, we didn't cut down trees—and, before lighting the fire, we checked that there wasn't a strong wind—a common mistake—that could spread the sparks. We lit the bonfire carefully—using paper and some small kindling—and we always had a bucket of water on hand—just in case—ready for any eventuality. We enjoyed the warmth and the stories, but safety was, without a doubt, our number 1 priority.

text_es: When building a safe campfire for environmental protection, be sure to choose a spot away from dry vegetation to avoid starting a fire, and even further away from buildings. Ensure the ground under the campfire is dirt or rock; never build a fire on grass or wood, and clear a firebreak circle of at least three meters. Before lighting the fire, have water, sand, or a fire extinguisher on hand in case of any unexpected situations. Use dry, clean firewood, avoiding anything containing plastic or other pollutants, to prevent excessive sparks and toxic smoke. Never leave a campfire unattended while it is burning, not even for a moment. Before leaving, be sure to completely extinguish the campfire, ensuring there are no embers remaining.
text_tgt_raw: 在為環境保護燃燒安全營火時，務必選擇遠離乾燥植被的地方，以避免引發火災，更要遠離建築物。確保營火下的地面是泥土或石頭，切勿在草地或木頭上生火，並清理出至少三公尺的環狀防火區。點火前，手邊要備有水、沙子或滅火器，以防任何意外狀況。使用乾燥、乾淨的柴火，避免含有塑膠或其他污染物質，以免產生過多火花和有毒煙霧。營火燃燒時，切勿讓它無人看管，即使只是片刻也不行。離開前，務必將營火完全熄滅，確保裡頭沒有任何餘燼。
base_en: When lighting a safe bonfire—something crucial for the environment—always choose a spot away from dry vegetation—that way you'll avoid fires—and buildings. Make sure the ground is dirt or stone—never grass or wood—and clear a perimeter of at least 3 meters around it—an effective firebreak zone. Have water, sand, or a fire extinguisher on hand—for any unexpected emergency—before lighting the fire. Use dry, clean firewood—without plastics or other polluting materials—to avoid excessive sparks and toxic smoke. Never leave the bonfire unattended—not even for an instant—and extinguish it completely before leaving—making sure no live embers remain.

text_es: Setting up a balanced aquarium ecosystem, a fascinating activity, actually involves several important steps. First, you must decide on the type of aquarium, whether it's a freshwater or saltwater tank, and its size; for beginners, we usually recommend at least 60 liters. Choosing an appropriate location is also a top priority, avoiding direct sunlight to prevent excessive algae growth. Next, sequentially lay the substrate (such as gravel or fine sand), and install the filtration system (either external or internal) and heater, adjusting the water temperature based on the species you wish to keep, typically between 24 and 26 degrees Celsius. Once the aquarium is filled with water pre-treated with a water conditioner, a several-week "cycling" process must be undertaken to allow nitrifying bacteria to establish stably, which is an extremely crucial step. Finally, you can gradually introduce fish and aquatic plants to avoid affecting water quality balance, and carefully observe their adaptation to the environment.
text_tgt_raw: 建立一個平衡的水族箱生態系統，這項迷人的活動，其實牽涉著幾個重要的步驟。首先，您必須決定水族箱的種類，究竟是淡水缸還是海水缸，以及它的尺寸；對於初學者來說，我們通常建議至少要有60公升。選擇一個適當的位置也為首要之務，要避開陽光直射的地方，以免藻類過度生長。接著，依序鋪設底砂（例如礫石或細沙），並安裝過濾系統（外置式或內置式皆可）和加溫器，根據您想飼養的物種來調整水溫，通常介於攝氏24至26度之間。當水族箱裡灌滿了預先用淨水劑處理過的水後，便要進行數週的「養水」過程，讓硝化細菌得以在此穩定建立，這為一個極為關鍵的步驟。最後，才能逐步放入魚隻和水生植物，以避免影響水質平衡，並細心觀察牠們在這裡的適應狀況。
base_en: Setting up an aquarium—a fascinating activity—involves several essential steps to create a balanced aquatic ecosystem. Initially, you must select the type of aquarium—freshwater or marine—and its size—at least 60 liters is recommended for beginners. Location is key—away from direct sunlight—to prevent excessive algae growth. Subsequently, the substrate—gravel or sand—, the filtration system—external or internal—, and the heater are installed, adjusting the temperature according to the species—generally between 24 °C and 26 °C. Once filled with water—previously treated with conditioner—, the aquarium is cycled for several weeks to establish nitrifying bacteria—a vital process. Finally, fish, and plants are introduced gradually—to avoid disturbing the balance—, carefully observing their adaptation.

text_es: Three months ago, I embarked on my first fish-keeping adventure. That afternoon, it was pouring rain, and I was idly browsing online when I stumbled upon a fascinating video about marine life, and suddenly the idea of setting up an aquarium came to me. At first, my partner was a bit skeptical, but later enthusiastically joined the plan. We first decided on a suitable size; a 90-liter aquarium seemed perfect for me. Then, after two weeks of research, we selected our future little tenants. Buying decorations like rocks, aquatic plants, and driftwood was a lot of fun, though quite expensive. The most crucial "water cycling" process lasted a month, but the long wait was worth it. Finally, when we put six neon tetras and two corydoras into their new home, watching them swim freely inside was truly a relaxing sight.
text_tgt_raw: 三個月前，我踏上了人生的第一趟養魚冒險。那天午後下著傾盆大雨，我閒來無事上網瀏覽，無意間看到一段關於海洋生物的迷人影片，突然萌生了設置水族箱的念頭。起初，我的伴侶有些懷疑，但後來也熱情地加入了這個計畫。我們首先決定了合適的尺寸，90公升的水族箱對我來說似乎完美無比。接著，經過兩週的研究，我們選定了未來的小房客。採買岩石、水草和沉木等裝飾品非常有趣，雖然價格不菲。最關鍵的「養水」過程持續了一個月，但漫長的等待是值得的。最終，當我們將六隻霓虹燈魚和兩隻鼠魚放入牠們的新家時，看著牠們在裡頭悠游自在，那真是一種令人放鬆的景象。
base_en: 3 months ago, I embarked on the adventure of setting up an aquarium—my 1st ever. The idea came to me one afternoon—it was raining cats and dogs—while I was browsing the internet and saw a fascinating documentary about marine life. My partner—skeptical at 1st—joined the project with enthusiasm. The 1st thing was to choose the right size—a 90-liter seemed perfect to me—and, after 2 weeks of research, we decided which fish would be the tenants. Buying the decorations—rocks, plants, and a log—was fun, though a bit expensive. The cycling process—the most critical phase—lasted 1 month, but the wait was worth it when, finally, we introduced the 6 Chinese neon tetras and 2 corydoras, which now swim happily—a relaxing spectacle—in their new home.

text_es: When setting up an aquarium for the first time, patience is the key to success; this is an extremely crucial step. Before choosing fish and aquatic plants, be sure to thoroughly research their compatibility to ensure you can establish a balanced and healthy ecosystem. It is recommended to start with an aquarium of at least 60 liters, as this size is easier to maintain stable water quality. Before introducing any living organisms, you must wait for the nitrogen cycle in the tank to be completely established; this is a fundamental biological process that usually takes four to six weeks. Essential equipment for a freshwater aquarium should include an appropriate filter chosen according to the size of the aquarium (either internal or external), a necessary heater, and a thermometer. When feeding, offer small amounts and a variety of foods; do not overfeed, as this will lead to water quality deterioration. To maintain the aquarium in optimal condition, perform partial water changes regularly (weekly or bi-weekly).
text_tgt_raw: 初次設立水族箱時，耐心是成功的不二法門，這是極為關鍵的一步。在選擇魚隻與水草之前，務必詳盡研究牠們的相容性，以確保能建立一個平衡且健康的生態系統。建議從至少60公升的水族箱開始，這個大小較容易維持水質穩定。引入任何生物前，必須等待缸內的氮循環徹底完成，這是一個基礎的生物作用，通常需要四到六週的時間。這裡軟體水族箱裡不可或缺的設備，應包括一個依照水族箱大小選擇的適當過濾器（內置或外置皆可）、必要的加溫器以及溫度計。餵食時請少量多樣，切勿過度餵食，否則會導致水質惡化。為了維持水族箱的最佳狀況，請定期（每週或每兩週）進行部分換水。
base_en: When setting up an aquarium for the 1st time, patience is key—a crucial step. Research thoroughly the fish and plants you want—compatibility is vital—to ensure a balanced and healthy ecosystem. Start with a tank of at least 60 liters—a manageable size—to facilitate the stability of water parameters. The nitrogen cycle—a fundamental biological process—must be completed before introducing any animals; this can take 4 to 6 weeks. Make sure you've an adequate filter—internal or external, depending on the size—a heater if necessary, and a thermometer. Feeding should be varied and in small quantities—don't overfeed—to avoid water quality problems. Perform partial water changes regularly—every 1 or 2 weeks—to keep the aquarium in optimal condition.

text_es: Changing a tire, a seemingly troublesome process, is actually something everyone can easily learn. First, for safety, be sure to park the car on a flat surface and away from traffic; this is a very important first step. Next, before jacking up the car, slightly loosen the lug nuts on the tire, but remember not to remove them completely. Only after the car body is firmly supported can you completely remove the lug nuts and carefully take off the flat tire; here, be careful not to damage the axle. Then, put on the spare tire and tighten the lug nuts in a diagonal pattern to ensure even pressure. Finally, slowly lower the vehicle back to the ground and use a tool to fully tighten the lug nuts. After completing all of this, please check the spare tire's pressure as soon as possible and arrange to have the original flat tire repaired or replaced.
text_tgt_raw: 換輪胎，這個看似麻煩的過程，其實人人都能輕易學會。首先，為了安全起見，務必將車停在平坦且遠離車流的地方，這是非常重要的第一步。接著，在尚未將車頂高之前，先將輪胎上的螺帽稍微鬆開，但切記不要完全卸下。待車身已穩穩地撐起後，才能將螺帽完全取下，並小心地將爆胎的輪胎移開，這裡要注意別讓軸心受損。然後，將備用輪胎裝上，並以對角方式鎖緊螺帽，這樣才能確保受力均勻。最後，將車輛緩緩降回地面，並用工具將螺帽徹底鎖緊。完成這一切後，請儘速確認備胎的胎壓是否正常，並安排將原來的爆胎進行修復或更換。
base_en: Changing a flat tire—a common and inconvenient situation—is a process anyone can learn to do. The 1st step is to secure the vehicle—to prevent accidents—in a flat, safe place, away from traffic. Next, you must loosen the lug nuts—without removing them completely—before lifting the car with the jack. Once the vehicle is raised, completely remove the lug nuts and proceed to remove the flat tire—with caution to avoid damaging the axle. Afterward, place the spare tire and tighten the lug nuts diagonally—for uniform fastening. Finally, lower the car to the ground and firmly tighten the lug nuts—using the lug wrench with force—before putting away the tools. It's crucial to check the spare tire's pressure as soon as possible and repair or replace the flat tire.

text_es: I still remember the last time I changed a tire; it's an experience I'll never forget. That day, after working all day, I was driving home when I suddenly felt the car sway, and then it started to wobble. I quickly pulled the car over to the side of the road, afraid of obstructing oncoming traffic. When I got out, I saw that the front right tire was completely flat; it was a disaster. I took out the tool kit from the trunk, a kit I always keep ready for emergencies. Following the instructions, I started loosening the lug nuts, and honestly, it took a lot of effort. After about twenty minutes, longer than I expected, and with my hands covered in grease, I finally got the spare tire on and continued my journey, feeling incredibly relieved.
text_tgt_raw: 我還記得上一次換輪胎的經驗，那真是一輩子都忘不了。那天工作了一整天，正開車回家，突然感覺到車子晃了一下，接著就開始搖擺不定。我趕緊把車停到路邊，深怕妨礙到來往車輛，下車一看，發現右前輪完全癟了，簡直是個大災難。我從後車廂裡拿出工具組，這工具我總是準備著以備不時之需。依照說明，我開始鬆開螺絲，說實話，這過程真花了我不少力氣。大約過了二十分鐘，比我預期的還久，手上也沾滿了油污，總算把備胎換上，然後繼續我的旅程，心裡感到無比的輕鬆。
base_en: I remember the last time I had to change a flat tire—an experience I'll never forget. I was driving home—after a long day at work—when, suddenly, I felt a bump and the car started to swerve. I pulled over to the shoulder—being careful not to get in the way—and when I got out, I saw that the front right tire was completely flat—a total disaster. I took the tool kit out of the trunk—which I always keep ready—and, following the instructions, I started to loosen the bolts—with quite a bit of effort, to be honest. After about 20 minutes—longer than I expected—and with my hands dirty with grease, I managed to put on the spare tire and continue my journey—an immense relief.

text_es: As a driver, learning how to change a spare tire is a basic and important skill. First, be sure to park the vehicle in a safe, flat area away from traffic, engage the parking brake, turn on the hazard lights, wear a reflective vest, and place a warning triangle approximately fifty meters behind the car. Next, take out the spare tire, jack, and wrench, ensuring the spare tire is in good condition. Before using the jack to lift the car, slightly loosen the lug nuts, but do not remove them completely. Once the vehicle is lifted, fully remove the lug nuts, carefully take off the flat tire, and avoid damaging the bolts. Then, put on the spare tire, hand-tighten the lug nuts, lower the vehicle, and then use the wrench to securely tighten all lug nuts in a star-shaped, diagonal pattern. Finally, don't forget to check the tire pressure of the newly installed tire as soon as possible.
text_tgt_raw: 身為駕駛，學會換備胎是項基本且重要的技能。首先，務必將車輛停在安全平坦、遠離車流的區域，並拉起手煞車、開啟警示燈，同時穿上反光背心，並在車後約五十公尺處放置三角警示牌。接著，取出狀態良好的備胎、千斤頂和扳手。在用千斤頂將車身抬起前，先將輪胎螺絲稍微鬆開，但不要完全卸下。待車輛升起後，再將螺絲完全卸除，小心翼翼地取下爆胎，避免損壞螺栓。然後，裝上備胎，用手將螺絲鎖緊，接著放下車身，再以星狀對角方式用扳手確實鎖緊所有螺絲。最後，別忘了盡快檢查新換上輪胎的胎壓。
base_en: To change a flat tire—an essential skill for any driver—it's fundamental to follow some key steps. 1st, find a safe place—flat and away from traffic—to stop. Make sure to put on the handbrake and the emergency lights—they're mandatory—and put on the reflective vest and the pre-signaling triangles—at an adequate distance of 50 m. Afterward, take out the spare tire—it should always be in good condition—the jack, and the lug wrench. Loosen the nuts—without removing them completely—before lifting the car with the jack. Once the vehicle is raised, remove the nuts completely and take off the flat tire—being careful not to damage the studs. Place the spare tire, tighten the nuts by hand, and lower the car before tightening them firmly—in a star pattern—with the wrench. Don't forget to check the pressure of the new tire as soon as possible.

text_es: Visiting a museum with children can be both educational and inspiring if planned properly. To achieve this, it's crucial to select an exhibition hall or special exhibit whose content is suitable for their age and interests, as this will capture their attention from the start. Before heading out, it's a good idea to check online if the museum offers interactive activities, such as software guides, games, or worksheets specifically designed for children, as these usually best capture young children's attention. During the visit, set a predetermined visiting time with them, allowing them to explore freely within certain limits, which helps create a more relaxed atmosphere. Don't forget that it's very necessary to find a place for the children to rest and have a snack at appropriate times. Even more importantly, encourage them to ask questions at any time, or share what they saw here and there, thereby fostering curiosity, which is the cornerstone of learning. Through these methods, a museum trip will become a fun and highly inspiring adventure that will make them want to come again next time.
text_tgt_raw: 帶孩子參觀博物館，若能妥善規劃，將會是一趟兼具教育意義與啟發性的體驗。為此，選擇內容適合其年齡與興趣的展館或特展至關重要，如此才能從一開始就吸引他們的注意。出發前，不妨先上網查詢館方是否有提供互動式活動，諸如軟體導覽、遊戲或專為孩童設計的學習單等，因為這些通常最能抓住小孩子們的目光。在參觀過程裡，與他們預先設定好參觀時間，讓他們在一定限制內自由探索，這有助於營造更輕鬆的氛圍。別忘了在適當的時候，找個地方讓孩子們稍作休息並享用點心，這是非常必要的。更要鼓勵他們隨時提問，或分享這裡、那裡看到了什麼，藉此培養好奇心，這正是學習的基石。透過這些方式，博物館之行將會成為一場充滿樂趣又極具啟發性的冒險，讓他們下次還想再來。
base_en: Visiting a museum with children can be an experience—educational and enriching—if planned properly. It's essential to choose a museum—or an exhibition—that offers content adapted to their age and interests, as this will capture their attention from the 1st moment. Before going, it's useful to research the interactive activities—workshops, games, or specific guides—that the museum offers, as these are usually the most attractive for the little ones. Setting clear expectations—like the time that will be spent in each room—and allowing them to explore at their own pace—within certain limits—will contribute to a more relaxed atmosphere. Don't forget to include breaks for resting and snacking—something essential—and encourage them to ask questions or share their impressions about what they see, thus fostering their curiosity—a pillar of learning. In this way, a museum visit will become an adventure—fun and formative—that they'll want to repeat.

text_es: I remember one time, I took my two nephews, aged six and eight, to an interactive science museum. At first, I thought to myself that this would probably be a daunting task, destined to be a battle lost from the start, but it turned out I was happily mistaken. The moment they stepped inside, they were deeply captivated by the lifelike dinosaur models and space models, their eyes lighting up. They spent a full two hours there, full of endless energy, running from one exhibit hall to another, constantly pressing every button, and asking many profound questions. What surprised me most was that while they were playing with a Van de Graaff generator that made their hair stand on end, amidst their laughter, they actually developed an interest in physics, something I had never anticipated before. This was truly a wonderful experience, where I probably learned as much as they did, if not more.
text_tgt_raw: 我記得有一次，我帶著六歲和八歲的兩個姪子去參觀一間互動式科學博物館。一開始我心裡想著，這大概會是一項艱鉅的任務，註定會是一場從頭就輸掉的戰役，但事實證明我錯得很開心。他們一踏進去，就被那些栩栩如生的恐龍模型和太空模型深深吸引，眼睛為之一亮。他們在那裡花了整整兩個小時，充滿著用不完的精力，從一個展廳跑到另一個展廳，不停地按著每個按鈕，也問了好多很有深度的問題。最讓我驚訝的是，當他們玩著一台會讓頭髮豎起來的范德格拉夫起電機時，在歡笑聲中，竟然對物理產生了興趣，這是以前我從未預料到的。這真是一次很棒的經驗，在那裡，我學到的東西可能跟他們一樣多，甚至更多。
base_en: I remember once we decided to visit a science museum—one of those interactive ones—with my 2 nephews, ages 6 and 8. At 1st, I thought it would be a titanic task—a battle lost from the start—but I was pleasantly mistaken. As soon as they entered, their eyes lit up at the dinosaurs—impressive reconstructions—and the space models. They spent 2 whole hours running from one room to another—with inexhaustible energy—pressing all the buttons and asking questions non-stop—some very insightful. The most surprising thing was seeing how they became interested in physics—something I never expected—when playing with a Van de Graaff generator, which made their hair stand on end—amid laughter and shouts. It was a fantastic experience, one of those where you learn as much or more than they do.

text_es: When visiting a museum with children, especially young ones, planning ahead is key to success. First, it's a good idea to choose a museum or special exhibition that offers interactive activities or visually engaging themes. Before you go, you can talk to them about what they will see using pictures or videos, which will greatly increase their interest. The time spent in the museum should not be too long; one to two hours is sufficient to prevent children from feeling tired or overwhelmed, and to allow them to explore at their own pace. During the visit, feel free to ask open-ended questions, such as: "What in this painting catches your eye?" No matter how simple your child's observations are, respond enthusiastically. Don't forget to prepare some snacks and water; this can effectively prevent them from getting hungry too quickly, making the trip smoother. Most importantly, remember that the main purpose of this trip is for the whole family to enjoy quality time together and to spark your child's curiosity.
text_tgt_raw: 帶著孩子參觀博物館，尤其若是幼齡兒童，事前規劃是成功的關鍵。首先，選擇一間能提供互動式活動或視覺上引人入勝主題的博物館或特展，會是比較好的主意。出發前，可以先透過圖片或影片和他們聊聊將會看到什麼，這樣能大大提升他們的興趣。在館裡的時間不宜過長，一到兩小時就已足夠，避免孩子感到疲憊或不知所措，並讓他們能以自己的步調探索。過程中，不妨多問開放式問題，例如：「這幅畫裡有什麼東西吸引你的目光呢？」無論孩子的觀察多麼簡單，都要熱情地回應。別忘了準備一些小點心和水，這能有效防止他們過快感到飢餓，讓旅程更加順暢。最重要的是，要記得此行的主要目的為全家人一起享受親子時光，並啟發孩子的好奇心。
base_en: For a museum visit with children—especially if they're young—to be a success, planning is key. Choose a museum—or a specific exhibition—that offers interactive activities or visually appealing themes for their age. Before going—this will increase their interest—you can talk about what they'll see or even look up some images. Limit the duration of the visit—1 or 2 hours is enough so they don't get overwhelmed—and let them explore at their own pace. Ask open-ended questions—"What catches your eye in this painting?"—and respond enthusiastically to their observations, however simple they may seem. Bring a small snack and water—essential to prevent them from getting tired quickly—and, above all, remember that the main goal is to enjoy yourselves as a family and spark their curiosity.

text_es: Organizing your closet, a seemingly simple yet important task, goes far beyond just folding clothes. It requires thorough planning to effectively utilize space and make various items, from T-shirts to coats, easily accessible. First, we should empty everything from the closet, which is also a good time to discard clothes no longer used and thoroughly clean the interior. Next, categorize clothes by type (such as tops, pants, underwear) and season; items not needed for the current season can be stored in dedicated storage bins or breathable bags. For clothes that need to be hung, like shirts or dresses, it's recommended to use uniform hangers, which not only saves space but also makes the overall look more aesthetically pleasing. Finally, categorizing clothes by color or style helps us quickly find the specific item we need, resulting in a practical and visually appealing closet, which is definitely a worthwhile investment.
text_tgt_raw: 整理衣櫥這個看似簡單卻又重要的任務，遠不只侷限於折疊衣物。它需要我們周詳的規劃，才能有效利用空間，並方便取用從T恤到大衣等各式衣物。首先，我們應將衣櫥裡所有物品清空，這也是一個丟棄不再使用衣物的好時機，同時也能徹底清潔內部。接著，將衣物依照類別（如上衣、褲子、內衣褲）和季節進行分類，那些當季用不著的，便可收納於專用收納箱或透氣袋裡。至於需要吊掛的衣物，像是襯衫或洋裝，建議使用統一的衣架，不只節省空間，也能讓整體視覺更為美觀。最後，將衣物依顏色或款式歸類，有助於我們快速找到所需的單品，如此一來，便能擁有一個實用且賞心悅目的衣櫥，這絕對是一項值得的投資。
base_en: Organizing your closet—an essential task—involves more than just folding clothes. It requires careful planning to optimize space and facilitate access to our garments—from t-shirts to coats. The 1st step is to completely empty the closet—a good time to discard what you don't use—and clean its interior. Then, you should sort clothes by category—such as blouses, pants, underwear—and by season, storing what you won't use in special boxes or bags—ideally breathable. For hanging clothes—like shirts or dresses—it's recommended to use uniform hangers to save space and improve aesthetics. Finally, grouping garments by color or type helps you find what you're looking for quickly, thus achieving a functional and visually appealing closet—a worthwhile investment of time.

text_es: Last Sunday, I finally made up my mind to organize my closet, a task I always put off again and again. I started taking out all the clothes one by one; it was practically a mountain of clothes, and I had to decide what to keep and what to donate. During the organizing process, I discovered I actually had three almost identical sweaters, which is a puzzling habit, and two pairs of pants I hadn't worn in five years. Although it was a slow and somewhat nostalgic process, I ultimately succeeded in clearing out more than half of the space in my closet. Now, I can finally clearly see all my clothes, which is a miracle! I no longer have to rummage through everything every morning to find clothes, and I feel 10% more efficient. Next time, hopefully in six months, I promise not to accumulate so many things again.
text_tgt_raw: 上週日，我終於下定決心整理衣櫃，這件總是被我一再推遲的任務。我開始將所有衣服一件件地拿出來，那簡直是一座衣物山，我得決定哪些要留下，哪些可以捐出去。在整理的過程裡，我發現自己竟然有三件幾乎一模一樣的毛衣，真是個令人費解的習慣，還有兩條五年沒穿過的褲子。雖然這是一個緩慢且帶點懷舊感的過程，但我最終還是成功清出了衣櫃裡的一大半空間。現在，我終於可以清楚看見自己所有的衣物，這真是一個奇蹟！再也不必每天早上翻箱倒櫃地找衣服，感覺效率提升了百分之十。下次，希望是六個月後吧，我保證不再累積這麼多東西了。
base_en: Organizing my closet—a task I always postpone—was last Sunday's mission. I started taking out all the clothes—a mountain of garments—deciding what to keep and what to donate. I realized I had 3 almost identical sweaters—an incomprehensible habit—and 2 pairs of pants I hadn't worn in 5 years. It was a slow process—and somewhat nostalgic—but I finally managed to clear a large part of the space. Now I can see everything I've got—a miracle!—and I don't have to rummage every morning, which is 10% more efficient. Next time—in 6 months, I hope—I promise not to accumulate so much.

text_es: To tackle the seemingly daunting task of organizing your closet, first empty everything out of it. As you take out each item of clothing, honestly assess whether you still use it, if it fits, and if it's comfortable to wear. Discard clothes you no longer need, such as old or damaged items; donate those in good condition, and consider recycling items that are no longer wearable. Next, group your clothes by type, such as T-shirts, pants, dresses, and then further subdivide them into summer or winter wear. Utilize soft tools like storage boxes and drawer dividers within your closet to maximize vertical space and keep everything tidy. Hang shirts that wrinkle easily and delicate tops on hangers, and neatly fold and store the rest. Remember, a well-organized closet not only saves you valuable time, especially when you're rushing out the door every morning, but also extends the lifespan of your clothes.
text_tgt_raw: 要整理衣櫃這項看似浩大的工程，首先要將裡面的東西全部清空。拿出每件衣物時，請誠實評估它是否仍在使用、是否合身、以及穿著時是否舒適。對於不再需要的衣物，例如老舊或破損的，請丟棄；狀況良好的可以捐贈，而不能再穿的則考慮回收。接著，將衣服依照類型分組，像是T恤、褲子、洋裝等，然後再細分為夏季或冬季服飾。利用衣櫃裡的收納盒、抽屜分隔板等軟體工具，充分利用垂直空間，讓一切保持整齊。容易皺的襯衫和精緻上衣請用衣架掛起來，其餘的則整齊摺疊收好。請記住，一個井然有序的衣櫃不僅能節省您寶貴的時間，特別是每天早上趕著出門時，也能延長衣物的壽命。
base_en: To organize your closet—a task that can seem overwhelming at 1st—start by emptying it completely. Evaluate each garment—be honest with yourself—and decide if you use it, if it fits you well, and if it makes you feel comfortable. Discard what you don't need—old or damaged clothes—donating what's in good condition or recycling what's unusable. Group clothes by type—T-shirts, pants, dresses—and then by season—summer and winter. Use internal organizers—boxes, drawer dividers—to take advantage of vertical space and keep everything tidy. Hang what wrinkles easily—shirts, delicate blouses—and fold the rest compactly. Remember that an organized closet not only saves time—especially in the mornings—but also extends the life of your clothes.

text_es: Canning tomatoes is a time-honored culinary technique that allows perfectly ripe tomatoes to be preserved for later enjoyment. The process generally goes like this: first, fully ripe tomatoes are selected, pear-shaped varieties being preferred, then they are washed clean and briefly blanched to facilitate peeling—a task that can sometimes be laborious—and then the seeds are removed. The prepared tomatoes are crushed or chopped according to the desired consistency, then simmered over low heat, usually with a little salt added, and perhaps a few basil leaves for flavor. Once the sauce is cooked, it must be poured into sterilized glass jars—which is extremely important for food safety—and then pasteurized, usually by heating in a water bath, to create a vacuum and ensure long-term preservation. If stored in a cool, dark place, they can even be kept for over a year.
text_tgt_raw: 製作罐裝番茄是一項源遠流長的烹飪技藝，它讓成熟度最佳的番茄得以保存，方便日後享用。這個過程大致上是這樣的：首先挑選熟透的番茄，梨形品種為佳，接著將其清洗乾淨，並短暫汆燙以方便去皮——這工作有時挺費力的——然後再去除種籽。處理好的番茄會依照所需的濃稠度，壓碎或切塊，接著用小火慢煮，通常會加點鹽，或許再放幾片羅勒葉來提味。醬汁煮好後，必須裝入消毒過的玻璃罐裡——這對於食品安全極為重要——然後進行巴氏殺菌，通常是隔水加熱，好形成真空，確保能長期保存。如果存放在陰涼避光的地方，甚至可以保存超過一年。
base_en: Making canned tomatoes is a culinary technique—deeply rooted in many cultures—that allows the fruit to be preserved—at its optimal point of ripeness—for later consumption. The basic process involves selecting ripe tomatoes—ideally of the pear variety—washing them, briefly blanching them to easily peel them—a task that can be laborious—and removing the seeds. Afterward, they're crushed or cut into pieces—depending on the desired consistency—and cooked over low heat, often with a little salt and perhaps a few basil leaves—to enhance the flavor. Once the sauce is cooked, it's packed into sterilized glass jars—this is fundamental for food safety—and then pasteurized—generally using a bain-marie—to create a vacuum and ensure long preservation, which can exceed 1 year if stored in a cool, dark place.

text_es: Every late summer, my favorite time of year, my parents and I would begin our family tradition of canning tomatoes. This is a time I cherish deeply, and it all starts with buying twenty kilograms of the freshest, plumpest, and juiciest ripe tomatoes from a friend's garden. The process is arduous, taking about eight hours, but we enjoy every minute of it. We blanch and peel the tomatoes—a tedious but necessary step—then process them into a thick puree using a machine. Next, we simmer this tomato sauce over low heat, adding basil and salt, until the sauce reduces to its perfect consistency. By evening, we will have finished fifteen to twenty jars of delicious homemade tomato sauce, whose incomparable flavor will see us through the entire winter, allowing us to enjoy this wonderful treat in our cozy home, even if there's no internet or bus service there.
text_tgt_raw: 每年夏末，那是我最愛的時節，我父母與我總會展開製作番茄罐頭的家族傳統。這是我非常珍視的時刻，一切從向朋友的菜園購買二十公斤最新鮮、紅潤多汁的成熟番茄開始。製作過程雖然艱辛，耗時約八小時，但我們樂在其中。我們會將番茄汆燙、去皮——這雖然是繁瑣卻必要的步驟——然後透過機器製成濃稠的果泥。接著，我們將這番茄醬以小火慢煮，加入羅勒與鹽，直到醬汁濃縮至最完美的狀態。到了傍晚，我們便能完成十五到二十罐美味的自製番茄醬，那無可比擬的風味，將能伴我們度過整個冬天，即使那裡沒有網路或公車，我們也能在這溫馨的家裡享受著這份美好。
base_en: Each year, towards the end of summer—my favorite time, without a doubt—my parents and I embark on the ritual of making canned tomatoes. It's a family tradition—something I cherish greatly—that begins with buying 20 kg of ripe tomatoes—the best, from a friend's garden—red and juicy. The process is laborious—about 8 hours of work—: we blanch the tomatoes, peel them—a tedious but necessary task—and pass them through the machine to obtain a thick purée. Then, we slowly cook this sauce—over low heat—with basil and salt, until it reduces to perfection. At the end of the day, we've 15 or 20 jars of delicious homemade tomato—an incomparable flavor—ready to use throughout the winter.

text_es: Making tomato sauce at home is a very rewarding experience. To ensure satisfactory results, first select fresh, ripe, and in-season tomatoes that have no bruises or blemishes. After carefully washing these tomatoes, without using detergent, quickly blanch them in boiling water for about 30 seconds. This will allow you to easily remove the tomato skins. Then, depending on the desired consistency of your sauce or puree, crush or chop the tomatoes and simmer them slowly over low heat, adding salt to taste according to your preference, until thickened. To ensure these tomato sauces can be safely preserved and to avoid potential risks, it is crucial to sterilize all jars and lids beforehand by boiling them in water for at least ten minutes. Finally, while hot, pour the cooked tomato sauce into hot jars, remembering to leave one to two centimeters of space at the top. After tightening the lids, place them in hot water for a water bath, according to the type of sauce you made, to create a vacuum seal, ensuring these delicious tomato sauces can be stored for at least twelve months or more.
text_tgt_raw: 自己在家裡製作番茄醬，是非常有成就感的一件事，為確保成果令人滿意，首先要挑選新鮮、成熟且當季的番茄，上面不能有任何擦傷或瑕疵。將這些番茄仔細洗淨後，無須使用清潔劑，接著把它們快速放入沸水裡汆燙約30秒，這樣能輕鬆地去除番茄皮。然後，根據您想要的醬汁或泥的濃稠度，將番茄壓碎或切塊，再用小火慢慢熬煮，其間可依個人喜好加入鹽巴調味，直到濃稠為止。為了確保這些番茄醬能夠安全保存，並且避免潛在的風險，事前將所有的瓶罐和瓶蓋進行消毒是至關重要的，可以將它們放入沸水中煮至少十分鐘。最後，趁熱將煮好的番茄醬裝入熱瓶中，記得在瓶口留下一到兩公分的空間，將瓶蓋旋緊後，再依據您製作的醬料類型，將其放入熱水裡進行水浴處理，以產生真空密封效果，確保這些美味的番茄醬至少能保存十二個月以上。
base_en: When venturing into the world of tomato preserves—a very rewarding practice—it's essential to start with fresh, ripe tomatoes—preferably in season—free of bruises or blemishes. Wash them well—without using detergents—and blanch them briefly in boiling water—about 30 seconds—to peel them easily. Then, crush, or cut them according to the desired consistency for your sauce or puree, and cook them over low heat—adding salt to taste—until they thicken. It's crucial to sterilize the jars and lids—this is vital—by boiling them for at least 10 minutes to ensure preservation and avoid risks. Fill the hot jars with the hot tomato, leaving 1-2 cm of headspace to the rim, seal them tightly, and process them in a water bath—depending on the type of preserve—to create a vacuum seal, guaranteeing their durability for 12 months or more.

text_es: Learning the fascinating art of photography is about more than just owning a high-end camera; technology and creativity are at its core. First, you must understand basic principles like exposure, ISO, aperture, and shutter speed, which control the light entering the sensor. Composition, the way elements are organized within the frame, is equally crucial for capturing compelling images, so studying rules like the rule of thirds or symmetry will be very helpful. Whether outdoors or in a studio, consistent practice is essential for developing a good photographic eye and refining your skills. Furthermore, learning post-processing software, such as Adobe Lightroom or Photoshop, is for improving the final result, as digital image editing is an indispensable part of modern photography. Finally, exploring different photography genres, from portraits to landscapes or street photography, can help you discover new ways of expression and gradually shape your own style.
text_tgt_raw: 學習攝影這門迷人的技藝，遠不止於擁有一台高階相機，其中技術與創意才是核心。首先，你必須理解曝光、ISO、光圈和快門速度等基本原理，它們控制著進入感光元件的光線。構圖，也就是在畫面裡組織元素的方式，對於拍出引人入勝的影像同樣關鍵，因此研究三分法則或對稱等規則將大有助益。不論是在戶外還是攝影棚裡，持續練習對於培養良好的攝影眼與精進技術都至關重要。此外，學習後製軟體，例如Adobe Lightroom或Photoshop，為的是改善最終成果，數位影像編輯在現代攝影裡是不可或缺的一環。最後，探索不同攝影類型，從人像到風景或街頭攝影，能讓你發掘新的表達方式，並逐漸形塑出自己的風格。
base_en: Learning photography—a fascinating discipline—involves much more than just owning a high-end camera, as technique and creativity are fundamental. Start by understanding the basic principles—such as exposure, ISO, aperture, and shutter speed—that control the light reaching the sensor. Composition—the art of organizing elements within the frame—is equally crucial for capturing attractive images, so studying rules like the rule of thirds or symmetry is very useful. Constant practice—whether outdoors or in a studio—is essential for developing a good photographic eye and perfecting technical skills. Furthermore, it's advisable to learn about post-processing—the digital editing of images—to improve the final result, using programs like Adobe Lightroom or Photoshop. Finally, exploring different photographic genres—from portraits to landscapes or street photography—allows you to discover new forms of expression and find your own style.

text_es: Bicycle maintenance is crucial for its safety, durability, and optimal performance. This involves a series of daily and regular upkeep tasks to ensure all key components function properly. For example, tire pressure, brake condition, and chain tension should be checked regularly, as they are essential for riding safety. To this end, it is recommended to frequently clean, lubricate, and adjust the derailleur, brakes, and steering system to prevent premature wear. Furthermore, it is very important to check that screws, nuts, and quick releases are tightened to prevent accidents. A visual inspection of the wheels, frame, and fork can reveal potential damage or cracks that need attention. Through these simple tasks, the bicycle's lifespan can be extended, while also ensuring users enjoy a more pleasant, efficient, and safe riding experience, no matter where you are, and online videos often provide related software tools to assist.
text_tgt_raw: 維護自行車對於其安全、耐用性及最佳性能而言至關重要。這其中牽涉到一系列的日常與定期保養，以確保各個關鍵零件運作正常。例如，胎壓、煞車狀況及鏈條張力都應規律檢查，因為它們是騎乘安全的必要環節。為此，建議經常清潔、潤滑並調整變速器、煞車與轉向系統，藉此預防過早磨損。此外，檢查螺絲、螺帽和快拆是否鎖緊也十分重要，以防意外發生。對輪組、車架和前叉進行目視檢查，則可發現需要留意的潛在損傷或裂痕。透過這些簡單的任務，自行車的壽命將能延長，同時也能確保使用者享有更愉悅、高效且安全的騎乘體驗，不論你身處何處，網路上的影片也時常提供相關的軟體工具來協助。
base_en: Maintaining a bicycle is crucial for its safety, durability, and optimal performance. It involves a series of routine and periodic care to ensure the proper functioning of its essential components. Tire pressure, brake condition, and chain tension should be checked regularly, as they're vital elements for safe riding. To do this, it's advisable to frequently clean, lubricate, and adjust the gears, brakes, and steering, thus preventing premature wear. It's also essential to check that the screws, nuts, and quick releases are properly tightened to prevent accidents. A visual inspection of the wheels, frame, and fork can reveal possible damage or cracks that need attention. With these simple tasks, the bicycle's lifespan is extended, and a more pleasant, efficient, and safe cycling experience is guaranteed for the user.

text_es: To begin basic bicycle maintenance, we will primarily focus on three key elements: cleaning, lubrication, and regular inspection. After each ride, be sure to use water, soap, and a brush to clean the frame, wheels, and all components, thoroughly removing any attached mud and dust. Pay special attention to the chain, cassette, and chainrings, as their cleanliness directly impacts their overall lifespan. As for chain lubrication, it is recommended to apply a specialized lubricant approximately every one hundred kilometers, or every fifteen days, or whenever you notice abnormal noise from the chain, ensuring the lubricant penetrates every corner of the chain links. For your safety and comfort while riding, regularly checking tire pressure, brake adjustments, and the condition of all cables, screws, and quick releases are all very important steps. By learning these three basic tasks, you will be able to enjoy cycling more fully, reduce breakdowns, and save money, time, and hassle on repairs. If you encounter any difficulties during the maintenance process, there are many online tutorial videos you can refer to, or you can ask experienced friends, or even directly seek assistance from a professional technician for more in-depth adjustments.
text_tgt_raw: 要開始自行車的基礎保養，我們主要聚焦在三個關鍵要素：清潔、潤滑與定期檢查。每次騎乘完畢，請務必用清水、肥皂與刷子清潔車架、輪組及各項零件，將附著在上面的泥土、灰塵徹底清除。特別是鏈條、飛輪和齒盤這些地方，它們的清潔程度會直接影響整體使用壽命。至於鏈條的潤滑，建議每騎乘約一百公里，或者每十五天，又或著當您感覺鏈條發出異常噪音時，就應該使用專用潤滑劑保養，確保潤滑油能深入到鏈節的每個角落。為了您騎乘時的安全與舒適，定期檢查胎壓、煞車調整狀況，以及各條纜線、螺絲和快拆是否完好，都是非常重要的環節。學會這三項基礎任務，您將能更盡情地享受騎車樂趣，減少故障發生，同時也節省了維修所需的金錢、時間與麻煩。如果在保養的過程裡遇到任何疑難雜症，這裡有許多網路上的教學影片可以參考，或是可以請教有經驗的朋友，甚至直接找專業技師協助做更深層的調整。
base_en: To start with bicycle maintenance, focus on 3 key elements: cleaning, lubrication, and regular inspection. After each ride, clean the frame, wheels, and components with water, soap, and a brush, removing dirt, dust, and mud. Pay special attention to the chain, sprockets, and chainrings, as a clean chain extends the lifespan of these elements. Lubricate the chain with a specific product every 100 km, or every 15 days, or if you notice excessive noise, making sure the lubricant penetrates the links well. Regularly check tire pressure, brake adjustment, and the general condition of cables, screws, and quick releases for your safety and comfort. Learning these 3 basic tasks will allow you to enjoy your bicycle more, reduce breakdowns, and save money, time, and trouble on repairs. If you've questions, consult tutorials, an expert friend, or a mechanic for more complex adjustments.

text_es: Hosting a successful farmer's market requires significant planning, effort, and coordination. First, an organizing committee must be established to handle the market's logistics, promotion, and management, which includes aspects like permits, regulations, and insurance. Choosing an ideal location is also crucial; it needs to be easily accessible, highly visible, and have enough space to accommodate stalls, visitors, and parking to attract a diverse and broad audience. Furthermore, the types of farmers, products, and services offered at the market must be clearly defined, with an emphasis on product variety, quality, and authenticity. Effective communication with farmers, the local community, and government agencies is essential for coordinating schedules, prices, and expectations. Promoting the market through media, the internet, and local events will attract more buyers, producers, and volunteers. Finally, daily operational management, including stall arrangement, customer service, and handling unexpected situations, will ensure a pleasant and productive experience for everyone.
text_tgt_raw: 舉辦一個成功的農夫市集，需要投入大量的規劃、心力與協調。首先，必須成立籌備委員會，負責市集的物流、宣傳及管理，其中涵蓋了許可證、法規和保險等面向。選擇理想的地點也至關重要，那裡需要交通便利、顯眼易見，並有足夠的空間容納攤位、遊客與停車，才能吸引多元的廣大群眾。此外，市集裡將提供的農戶種類、產品與服務也必須明確定義，著重於產品的豐富性、品質與真實性。與農戶、當地社區和政府機關進行有效的溝通，對於協調時間表、價格和期望至關重要。透過媒體、網路和地方活動來推廣市集，將能吸引更多買家、生產者和志工。最後，每日的營運管理，包括攤位安排、客戶服務以及處理突發狀況，將確保為每個人帶來愉快且富有成效的體驗。
base_en: Organizing a farmers market requires considerable planning, effort, and coordination for its success. 1st, it's essential to establish an organizing committee that will be in charge of the logistics, promotion, and management of the event, covering aspects such as permits, regulations, and insurance. The selection of the ideal location, one that's accessible, visible, and has enough space for stalls, visitors, and parking, is crucial to attract a broad and diverse public. In addition, the type of farmers, products, and services that will be offered must be defined, seeking variety, quality, and authenticity in the offerings. Effective communication with farmers, the local community, and authorities is vital to coordinate schedules, prices, and expectations. Promoting the market through media, social networks, and local events will attract buyers, producers, and volunteers. Finally, day-to-day management, including stall arrangement, customer service, and resolving unforeseen issues, will ensure a pleasant and productive experience for everyone.

text_es: When I first organized a farmers market, to be honest, I had no idea what challenges I would face. At that time, I naively thought it would be as simple as setting up a few tables, bringing some fruits, vegetables, and bread. However, I soon discovered it was a daunting task, involving various permits, logistical arrangements, and promotional activities. We had to contact farmers one by one, clearly explain the terms of cooperation, and ensure their willingness to participate, which truly required immense patience, excellent social skills, and extensive communication. Finally, we chose to hold the first market in a local park, surrounded by green trees, flowers, and grass, creating a very warm atmosphere. That day was a great success; everyone enthusiastically purchased fresh tomatoes, lettuce, and various cheeses, with nearly ninety percent of the stalls selling out. Seeing the community respond so enthusiastically, highly appreciating the quality of local produce and the opportunity for direct interaction, was an incredible experience. Through this organizing effort, I deeply realized that many wonderful things can be achieved with dedication, hard work, and goodwill.
text_tgt_raw: 第一次籌辦農夫市集時，老實說，我根本不知道自己將面臨什麼挑戰。那時候我還天真地以為，這不過就是擺幾張桌子、帶些水果蔬菜和麵包這麼簡單。然而，很快我就發現這是一項艱鉅的任務，裡頭牽涉著各種許可、物流安排和宣傳推廣等繁瑣事務。我們必須逐一聯繫農友，向他們清楚說明合作條件，並確保他們願意參與，這著實需要極大的耐心、高超的交際手腕以及大量的溝通。最後，我們選在一個當地公園裡舉辦了第一次市集，周圍環繞著綠樹、鮮花和草地，營造出非常溫馨的氣氛。那一天非常成功，大家熱情地採購新鮮番茄、生菜和各式乳酪，將近九成的攤位都銷售一空。看到社區如此熱烈地響應，對在地農產品的品質與直接互動機會給予高度肯定，這真是令人難以置信的經驗。透過這次的籌辦，我深刻體認到，只要懷抱著奉獻、努力與善意，很多美好的事物都是可以實現的。
base_en: The 1st time I set out to organize a farmers market, honestly, I didn't know what I was getting myself into. I remember thinking it would be something simple, like setting up some tables, bringing fruits, vegetables, and bread, and that's it. However, I soon discovered that it involved an arduous process: permits, logistics, and promotion, among many other things. We had to contact the farmers, explain the conditions to them, and ensure their participation, which required patience, diplomacy, and a lot of communication. We set up the 1st market in a local park, surrounded by trees, flowers, and grass, creating a very welcoming atmosphere. The day was a success, with people buying fresh tomatoes, lettuce, and cheeses, and 90% of the stalls selling everything. It was incredible to see the community's response, appreciating the local product, the quality, and the direct interaction. I learned that, with dedication, effort, and goodwill, great things can be achieved.

text_es: To successfully host a farmer's market, you must first start by researching locations, permits, and local regulations. Choosing a venue that is easily accessible, safe, and highly visible is crucial for customers, farmers, and vendors alike. Establish a clear vision, mission, and values for the market, aiming to promote sustainability, community engagement, and healthy eating. Next, contact local farmers, artisans, and food producers to ensure the market can offer diverse and high-quality products, such as fresh produce and artisanal bread. Promote the market through social media, flyers, and community events to attract buyers, sellers, and visitors. At the same time, consider the necessary infrastructure, such as tables, canopies, and clear signage.
